policy_title: Freeze Rail Fares and Simplify Ticketing
stated: Freeze rail fares and simplify ticketing on public transport to ensure regular users are paying fair and affordable prices. Make rail a genuinely convenient, affordable and environmentally-friendly option for both passengers and freight by: Urgently establishing a new Railway Agency.

source.quote: Freeze rail fares and simplify ticketing on public transport to ensure regular users are paying fair and affordable prices. Make rail a genuinely convenient, affordable and environmentally-friendly option for both passengers and freight by: Urgently establishing a new Railway Agency: a public body which would help to join up the industry – from track to train – putting commuters first, holding train companies to account, and bringing in wholesale reform of the broken fare system.

bearing_set.reason: Freezing rail fares directly reduces a recurring household travel cost for commuters and regular users, with a non-negligible effect on real disposable income and affordability of essentials-adjacent expenditure.

Explicitly framed as making rail an 'environmentally-friendly option'; lower fares plausibly shift modal share from car and air to rail, with a concrete emissions-reduction mechanism via reduced road/aviation use.

Freezing fares below inflation compresses revenue, widening the gap between passenger income and operating costs and requiring larger public subsidy or reduced network investment — a direct fiscal sustainability mechanism.

Lower, simpler fares expand access to labour markets and economic opportunity; the explicit freight dimension could reduce logistics costs and improve supply-chain productivity, both genuine aggregate-prosperity effects.

membership_note: Four fundamentals clear the non-negligible bar: the fare freeze is a direct cost-of-living relief (O2), an environmental lever via modal shift (O6), a fiscal liability via subsidy expansion (O12), and a productivity/opportunity enabler via access and freight (O13).
